was: Small Manitoba Provincial Park campground on Brereton Lake in the Whiteshell - 28 sites (8 with 15/30-amp electric, 20 non-serviced); playground and picnic shelters; store and restaurant at the adjacent Brereton Lake Resort. Open mid-May to Sept long weekend; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

was: Boise NF (Mountain Home RD) campground on Anderson Ranch Reservoir, ~14 mi north of Hwy 20 via Forest Hwy 61. 9 overnight drive-in sites (plus 18 day-use sites), vault toilets and potable water; no hookups. Curlew boat ramp with dock is adjacent. Good smallmouth bass and kokanee fishing. Open late May to end of September (snow dependent). --Claude

was: Salmon-Challis NF (Lost River RD), wooded setting along Star Hope Creek in the Copper Basin Loop area; reached via Trail Creek Rd + Copper Basin Rd/Loop (long maintained gravel). 21 units, 2 hand pumps (summer water), 3 vault toilets. Open Memorial Day weekend to end of Sep. --Claude

was: 8 sites along a small creek, Council RD (Hornet/Cuddy Mtn area), Payette NF; paved loop suited to medium RVs, vault toilets, no hookups. Typically open mid-May through Sept/early Oct. --Claude

was: Bonner County park on Garfield Bay of Lake Pend Oreille, across the road from a public boat launch. 29 RV sites + 14 tent sites in the trees; water available at sites but NO electric/sewer and no RV water hookup; 6 vault toilets. Open weekend before Memorial Day to weekend after Labor Day; reservable online, walk-ins welcome (cash/check). --Claude

was: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF campground on the shore of Washington Lake off the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (SR-150), elev ~10,000 ft. 43 sites (single/double family + group), concrete pads, picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no water on site. Mix of reservable-online and first-come sites; open roughly late June-mid Sept. Canoeing/kayaking/trout fishing on the lake. --Claude

was: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Logan Ranger District) on the mountainside above Tony Grove Lake ~19 mi E of Logan, elev ~8100 ft. 32 single + 1 double site, vault and flush toilets, no hookups; per rec.gov sites take RVs to 35 ft (tight turns favor smaller rigs). Reservable online, short season mid-July to late Sep. --Claude

was: Utah State Park campground at the edge of the coral-pink dune field NW of Kanab. 34 sites in two loops (old loop sites 1-22 no hookups; newer loop sites 23-34 water+electric) plus yurts; drive-in with paved loop roads, modern restrooms, dump station. Reservable online (4-month rolling window). --Claude

was: Fremont Indian SP campground in Sam Stowe Canyon along Clear Creek. 10 full-hookup sites (water, 30/50-amp, sewer) plus a large group RV site; flush restroom, coin showers, laundry; accommodates large RVs. Open year-round, reservable via ReserveAmerica. --Claude

was: Utah State Park at the south end of Millsite Reservoir near Ferron. 20-site campground: sites 1-10 power/water, 11-20 power-only, plus tent sites; mostly back-in with some pull-through to ~46 ft; picnic tables and grills. Reservable via ReserveAmerica (4-month window). --Claude

was: Utah State Park on Rockport Reservoir near Wanship. Six campgrounds (100+ sites): Juniper is the developed RV loop (23 sites w/ 30-amp electric & water, big rigs to ~40 ft, showers); others (Cottonwood, Crandall Cove, Twin Coves, Riverside, Pinery) are basic sites. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica. Pinned to Juniper loop on the E shore. --Claude

was: Weber County park in the South Fork Ogden River bottom below Causey Reservoir, east of Huntsville. 58 individual sites (fee paid on-site to the camp host) plus 5 group areas (A, B North, B South, C, Lodge -- reservable via Sportsites); an individual site takes one trailer + one tent; limited electricity in Areas B and C, otherwise dry camping; fire pits and picnic tables. Open first weekend of May to early October, weather permitting. --Claude

was: Weber County park on the east side of the Wasatch above Liberty/Eden, 2,600 acres. ~132 individual dry-camping sites across five areas (Cold Water, Cutler Flats, Loop A/B/Corrals, Middle Gate, Mustang Flats); fire pits, picnic tables, horse corrals. Travel trailers and pull-through sites are accommodated but the loop roads are narrow dirt, so it's best for smaller rigs; a 23-ft rig fits the drive-in sites. Group sites reservable. Open first weekend of May to mid-October, weather permitting. --Claude

was: Lutheran non-profit camp ~2 mi east of Long Valley Junction (US-89/SR-14) down a maintained gravel road, between Zion and Bryce; open to the public for nightly RV and tent camping May 1 to September 30. Large grassy RV spaces with water and 50-amp electric or full hookups, clubhouse and commercial kitchen, communal fire pit, restrooms and showers, cabins and bunkhouses. Reservations by phone, 800-205-4887. --Claude

was: Rustic family-run campground at 3000 S SR-24 in Caineville, ~20 min east of Capitol Reef NP; ~20 level pull-through sites for RVs and tents, 20/30/50-amp electric + water, clean restrooms with hot showers, dump station, big cottonwoods. Seasonal May-Sep; cell dead zone, reserve by phone (paper ledger). Camper-reported rate: $40 a night for 50-amp in October 2025, $35 in May 2024 (Campendium). --Claude

was: Oregon State Parks oceanfront campground on US-101 south of Waldport, right behind the beach dune. 32 electrical sites with water plus 42 tent sites and 2 yurts; max RV length listed to 40 ft. Reservable via ReserveAmerica; open seasonally mid-March to late October. Dump stations at South Beach or Washburne SP. --Claude

was: Oregon State Parks high-desert canyon campground on the John Day River. Sites 1-21 are large, spread-out drive-in sites with parking pad, table and fire ring (no electric/sewer hookups); drinking water and vault toilets plus a modern bathhouse with flush toilets/hot showers. Sites 22-28 are walk-in tent-only. 4 rustic cabins. Reservable; sites 1-21 go first-come, first-served Nov-Mar. --Claude

was: Oregon State Parks campground at the mouth of the Deschutes River near its Columbia confluence, off I-84. A-Loop has 34 electric/water sites with paved pads (rigs to ~55 ft); B-Loop has 14 primitive RV/tent sites; T-Loop tent and group camps. Reservable; A-Loop is first-come, first-served Dec-Mar, other loops closed in winter. Loop A has restrooms with hot showers. --Claude

was: Rustic USFS campground (Klamath NF, on the Siskiyou crest in Oregon) 1 mi south of Mt. Ashland Ski Resort, ~10.5 mi up FR 20 from I-5. 9 sites accommodating small RVs/trailers, pack-out trash. Open ~June-Oct once FR 20 clears of snow; elev ~6,600 ft. --Claude

was: USFS (Mt. Hood NF) at ~4,500 ft beside Olallie Meadow, reached via ~3 mi of gravel (FR 4690) then FR 4220. 7-site campground, open ~mid-June-mid-Sept (snow-gated). --Claude

was: 43 sites in two loops on the southeast shore of Timothy Lake, Mt. Hood NF, ~3,270 ft; 22 RV-sized non-electric sites plus 21 tent sites; vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov; open roughly Memorial Day through mid-September. --Claude

was: BLM (Burns District, Steens Mountain CMPA) campground on the shore of Fish Lake at ~7,400 ft among aspen and shore willow, ~17 mi up the Steens Mountain Loop Rd from Frenchglen. 23 sites, picnic tables + fire grates, vault toilet + drinking water, no hookups; max RV ~35 ft. Typically open early July-October per snowpack. High-clearance advised on parts of the loop road beyond, but the graded gravel loop to Fish Lake is passable to a 23-ft rig. --Claude
